name: Psychological Jujitsu: Hidden Favourites
summary: Players secretly bid cards from identical 1-13 hands for 13 prizes. A bid value matched by anyone is cancelled, the highest unique bid wins, and each player has a secret favourite prize value worth +5.

player.meaning: Cards still in this player's hand. The rules announce every hand each round.
Points won from prizes and bonuses
Secret bonus value, dealt at setup from bonus_pool and revealed at game end
Card bid this round, revealed once all bids are in
True when no other player bid the same value this round
True when this player won this round's prize
True when this player scored the +5 bonus this round

game.meaning: Prize values still in the pile. The remaining values are announced; the draw order is random.
Highest uncancelled bid this round; 0 if every bid was cancelled

setup: Every player's hand is set to the cards 1 to 13, and every score is set to 0.
The prize pile is set to the values 1 to 13.
Each player draws one value at random from bonus_pool into their bonus, and that value is removed from bonus_pool, so no two players share a bonus value.
Each player is privately told their own bonus value.

round.effect: round_no += 1. One value is drawn at random from prize_pile into prize and removed from prize_pile. Every player's bid_unique, won_round and bonus_scored are set to false, and winning_bid is set to 0.
Announce: 'Round {round_no}: the prize is {prize}.' Also announce every player's hand, every score and the prize_pile values still remaining.
Each player's message is set to their text. Then broadcast {"to": "all", "text": "Seat {seat} says: {value}"}. Messages are not binding.

round.answer: one card from your own hand
round.effect: Each player's bid is set to the chosen card. If a player gives an invalid answer or none, bid = the minimum of their hand.

Each player's bid is removed from their hand. For each player, bid_unique = (number of other players whose bid equals this bid) == 0. winning_bid = the maximum bid among players with bid_unique true, or 0 if no player has bid_unique true. For each player, won_round = bid_unique and bid == winning_bid.
For the player with won_round true: score += prize, and if prize == bonus, then score += 5 and bonus_scored = true.

Announce every player's bid, the winner of the prize (or 'cancelled: nobody scores' if winning_bid == 0) and the new scores. If bonus_scored is true for the winner, announce only '+5 bonus' together with the winner's new total, not the bonus value.
If round_no == 13, reveal every player's bonus to everyone and end the game. Otherwise continue with the next round.

ending.decided_by: Each player's standing is their final score. The highest score wins, and players tied at the top share the win (a draw among them).

rules.text: At setup, every player's hand is the 13 cards 1 to 13 and every score is 0.
At setup, each player gets a distinct bonus value drawn from {5,6,7,8,9}, and only that player can see it.
At the start of each round, one prize value is drawn at random from prize_pile, removed from it and announced, so each value 1 to 13 is a prize exactly once over 13 rounds.
Each round, every player sends one message of at most 40 words at the same time, and all messages are then shown to everyone.
Each round, every player secretly bids one card from their own hand at the same time, and no bid is seen until all are in.
When a player bids a card not in their hand, or gives no valid bid, then the lowest card in their hand is used as their bid.
After bidding, each player's bid card is removed from their hand permanently.
When two or more players bid the same value, all of those bids are cancelled.
The highest uncancelled bid wins the prize: with bids 10, 10 and 4, the player who bid 4 wins.
When every bid is cancelled (for example bids 7, 7 and 7), the prize is discarded and no score changes.
The winner adds the prize value to their score: winning a prize of 11 adds 11.
When the prize value equals the winner's bonus value, the winner adds 5 more: winning prize 7 with bonus 7 adds 12.
When a bonus is scored, the announcement says '+5 bonus' and the new total, but not the bonus value.
After round 13 the game ends and every bonus value is revealed.
The player with the highest final score wins, and players tied for the highest score share the win.

offers.question: Talk message
offers.options: a short free text of at most 40 words

offers.question: Bid
offers.options: exactly the cards remaining in that seat's own hand (13 options in round 1, falling by one each round to 1 option in round 13)

choices.why: The designer chose 3, so it is kept. Cancellation of matching bids needs at least 3 bidders to create the outbidding-by-colliding tension; with 2, any tie simply voids the round. The maximum stays at the source's 4, since more bidders make most rounds collapse into cancellations and drown out the hidden-favourite signal.

choices.what: Talk kept as a simultaneous poll with broadcast
choices.why: The source specifies simultaneous talk. Players genuinely disagree, since everyone wants the prize, so bluffing about intended bids or hinting at a favourite gives others something to reason about.

A thoughtful player avoids bids others are likely to duplicate, saves high cards for high prizes, uses talk to provoke collisions between rivals, and infers rivals' bonus values from how eagerly they chase mid prizes.
The rules announce every remaining hand each round, and hands are deducible from the revealed bids anyway.

simplifications.what: The shuffled face-down prize pile is modelled as a public list of remaining values with a random draw each round
simplifications.why: The rules announce the remaining prize values each round; only the order is hidden, and a random draw reproduces that.

simplifications.what: The '+5 bonus' announcement and the end-of-game bonus reveal are done with tell steps
simplifications.why: The bonus attribute stays visible only to its owner until the game ends.
